title: Earlier shared-year errors gave no clear low-runoff score gain at 221 NRCS sites in 2016-2025
abstract: We tested whether earlier error dependence improved forward forecasts of the mean regional low-runoff failure share in NRCS April 1 forecasts. We used a fixed panel of 221 sites in five drainage regions, with training from 2006 and testing in 2016-2025. A shared-year method kept all regional errors from one historical year together. Its reference chose a separate year per region. Both methods had exactly the same marginal distributions. We computed exact CRPS from all product scenarios. The shared-year method cut mean low-tail CRPS by 0.37%, with conditional 95% whole-year limits of -8.91 to +4.41%. Two-year blocks and earlier or fixed training gave no clear gain. A secondary high-tail test gave 14.49% gain, with limits of -6.85 to +26.45%. Thus the earlier full-record error alignment did not establish forward low-tail score skill for this method. This does not show independence or rule out useful dependence models. Ten test years, retrospective panel selection, revised archives and one scalar target limit inference. The package includes aggregate data, exact scores, code, source hashes and source regeneration instructions.

display.caption: Annual and mean CRPS gains from earlier shared-year errors. The primary low-runoff result gives no clear gain. Intervals resample paired annual scores and condition on fitted forecasts.
